comparator.name: Franse taal en cultuur
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines a complete 180-EC pathway with 60 EC in each year and no formal route. Year 1 combines four sequential French-language-acquisition modules with contemporary France, humanities, linguistics, literature and French language-and-state study. Year 2 contains French literature, French linguistics, a fifth language-acquisition module, philosophy of science, French cinema and a compulsory 30-EC semester in a French-speaking country. Year 3 contains a sixth French-language module, European literature, a French research workshop, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC graduation project. The official overview confirms the normalized identity, 180-EC load and RIO code 56808. Open choice space is preserved without invented content.

exception.reason: The UvA programme is defined by cumulative French-language acquisition and French-medium study. It develops speaking, listening, reading and writing through six compulsory language modules, integrates that competence with French linguistics, literature, cinema, culture and society, requires a 30-EC semester at a university in a French-speaking country, and culminates in a French research workshop and graduation project. UCR's current catalogue contains no French-language course at any level and no sustained sequence in French linguistics or French-language literature. UCR literature, media, history, politics and cultural-analysis courses can illuminate isolated comparative questions, but they cannot supply the French competence on which the study-abroad semester and advanced disciplinary work depend. A 24-course response would therefore be a broad European humanities and social-science programme without French, not a defensible closest match to French Language and Culture.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC of first-year French language, humanities, linguistics, literature and contemporary-France study; 30 EC of second-year taught study plus a compulsory 30-EC semester in a French-speaking country; and 18 EC of advanced third-year language, literature and research preparation, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC graduation project. No formal route is selected or combined, and genuine choice space remains open.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches French speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar or translation, and no course provides French linguistics or French-language literary study as its sustained disciplinary object. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide transferable literary and cultural analysis; MCCMEDI courses support film and media analysis; GOSHIST, GOSPOLI and GOSECON courses support historical, political and economic comparison; and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics examines language processing and acquisition generally. These courses could support comparative study of European culture, politics, history and representation, but they do not develop French proficiency or prepare students for French-medium coursework, a semester at a university in a French-speaking country and an independent graduation project grounded in French language and culture. Because the missing language sequence is the programme's academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent French Language and Culture programme.
